sections.h2: Where are Calhoun County land records filed?
sections.html:
Every land document for Calhoun County is recorded in Marshall, at the Clerk and Register of Deeds office in the County Building, 315 West Green Street. The Battle Creek office at 161 East Michigan Avenue handles circuit court filings and personal protection orders, so a deed carried there will not be recorded. The Marshall counter answers at 269-781-0718.

The research room, used by abstractors, title companies and genealogists, closes at 4:45 p.m., fifteen minutes before the office does. A drop box sits on the west side of the parking lot behind the County Building for completed documents that already have payment attached. Online, the county offers a record search and a property alert service for land records.

The staff cannot advise on how to fill out a land record form and keep no forms on hand. For help, the county points people to an attorney, the State Bar of Michigan referral line at 1-800-968-0738, or Michigan Legal Help.

sections.h2: What does Calhoun County charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The fee is $30 per document regardless of page count. It applies to deeds, mortgages, certified copies, lis pendens, timber, oil and gas leases, UCC filings, Land Division Act filings, discharges and terminations, and federal, state and employment security liens. Land record recordings are paid by cash or check only.

  • A discharge or assignment that covers several instruments adds $3 for each extra liber and page referenced.
  • The treasurer's tax certification for a warranty deed or land contract is $5.
  • Copies of real estate records run $1 per page, UCC copies $2 per page, and plat copies carry a $2 minimum per page.
  • Certifying any recorded instrument costs $5.

The statute behind the base fee is MCL 600.2567, which sets $30 for entering and recording a document and $3 for each additional instrument assigned or discharged.

sections.h2: Can I record a Calhoun County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, with one exception. Calhoun County takes e-recordings for every document type except papers that carry a real estate transfer tax valuation affidavit, which must be mailed or delivered to the Marshall office. A submitter uploads the document through a vendor, the register reviews it, and a rejected document goes back for correction before it is stamped and returned electronically.

The county works with four vendors: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. Contact one of them to register as a customer, and expect the vendor to offer demonstrations and training. When a document needs a tax certification, the system forwards it to the County Treasurer's Office for review, so the certificate does not need a separate trip.

sections.h2: What does the Marshall office check on a Calhoun County deed?
sections.html:
The county's posted checklist builds on MCL 565.201 and adds a few items that trip up sellers who prepare their own paper.

  • Original signatures with names typed or printed beneath them, and no mismatch against the notary acknowledgment.
  • A grantee street or post office address, and the name and address of the person who drafted the paper.
  • An acknowledgment by a judge, court clerk or Michigan notary.
  • A certified death certificate, recorded earlier and referenced by liber and page, whenever the deed says survivor.
  • Court orders certified and sealed by the clerk of the court.
  • One recordable event named on the first line, in 10-point black type on white 20-pound paper, with a 2 1/2 inch top margin on page one and 1/2 inch elsewhere.
  • The total value of the land on the face of the deed or a valuation affidavit attached. The deed must not rely on the phrase "and other good and valuable consideration."
  • Any transfer tax exemption written on the instrument, and a trust document recorded as its own separate paper.

sections.h2: Who certifies taxes before a Calhoun County warranty deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Calhoun County Treasurer does. Warranty deeds, land contracts, assignments of land contracts and any deed with a covenant of warranty need that office's tax certification before the register accepts them, and the fee is $5. The treasurer's office is in the same building at 315 West Green Street, open Monday through Thursday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Friday from 8 a.m. to noon. Call 269-781-0807 for deed certification.

The requirement traces to MCL 211.135. It calls for proof that no tax liens or tax titles are held against the parcel and that taxes have been paid for the five years before the deed's date. A deed with no warranty covenant, such as a plain quitclaim, is outside the rule.

Because the treasurer also collects delinquent real estate taxes for the county's 28 townships, cities and villages, a seller who has fallen behind will hear about it at this step. Settle the balance before the closing date so the certification does not hold up the recording.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies to a Calhoun County sale?
sections.html:
The combined rate is $4.30 per $500 of value, rounded up to the next $500: 55 cents for the county under MCL 207.504 and $3.75 for the state under MCL 207.525. The Calhoun County median owner-occupied value of $162,800 works out to 326 units of $500.

Calhoun County transfer tax at sample prices (statutory rates; $162,800 is the Census 2020-2024 median value)
Sale priceCounty taxState taxCombined
$75,000$82.50$562.50$645.00
$162,800$179.30$1,222.50$1,401.80
$300,000$330.00$2,250.00$2,580.00

Three exemptions matter most to people selling troubled property. The state act exempts a deed given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure on any mortgage, while the county act reaches only government-backed loans. Both acts exempt a court order that fixes no price. A deed to a child or grandchild is on the state list in MCL 207.526. Write the claimed exemption on the instrument itself.

sections.h2: What is Calhoun County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Calhoun County covers 718 square miles, 706 of them land, around Battle Creek, its largest city, and Marshall, the seat. Albion and Springfield are the other cities. The villages are Athens, Burlington, Homer, Tekonsha and Union City, and sixteen townships fill in the map. The county was established in 1829, organized in 1833, and anchors the Battle Creek metropolitan area.

Census QuickFacts counts 133,408 residents in 2025, down from 134,310 in 2020, across 59,808 housing units. About 72.7% of homes are owner occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $162,800 and median gross rent is $968. The county has 53,333 households with a median income of $63,177.

That value sits below the Cass County median of $218,000, so a Calhoun sale tends to carry a smaller transfer tax bill in dollars even though the rate is the same.

faqs.q: How much does recording a deed cost in Calhoun County?
faqs.a: Recording costs $30 per document, paid by cash or check. A discharge or assignment adds $3 for each additional liber and page it references, and a warranty deed also needs the $5 treasurer tax certification.

faqs.q: Can I record my deed at the Battle Creek office?
faqs.a: No. All land document recordings are filed in the Marshall office at 315 West Green Street. The Battle Creek location handles circuit court filings and personal protection orders.

faqs.q: Does Calhoun County accept e-recorded deeds?
faqs.a: Yes, through CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. The one exception is a document that has a transfer tax valuation affidavit attached, which has to be mailed or brought to the Marshall office.

faqs.q: Why would the Register of Deeds reject my deed?
faqs.a: Common reasons are a missing grantee address, no drafter name, signature names that differ from the acknowledgment, a missing property value, or a margin and type size that miss the statute. The office returns a rejected paper with the reasons checked off.

faqs.q: Who pays Calhoun County transfer tax on a home sale?
faqs.a: The statutes tax the instrument and do not assign the cost, so the purchase agreement decides. On a $162,800 sale the combined county and state tax is $1,401.80.
